title: Customer brief: quilt of micro-asks and runtime painnotes (June 2026)
content:
Purpose
Quick, pragmatic synthesis of repeating customer asks across May–June 2026 focused on runtime friction. I used a "quilt" metaphor: small, distinct asks stitched together that collectively increase operational overhead and product churn. This is an intentionally compact, actionable roll-up for eng triage and PM prioritization.

Topline summary (TL;DR)
- Most frequent themes: 1) KV cache miss patterns and ephemeral prefix reuse causing token spikes; 2) per-route observability and cost at token granularity; 3) rollout and fallback visibility (customers want deterministic behavior when a variant drops); 4) onboarding friction for Private (VPC) deployments — networking docs + checklist.

Representative customer quotes
- "Our latency blips are correlated to session rehydration — cache misses kill the SLA." — fintech integration lead
- "We need a bill preview for a route before scaling it up to 200 TPS." — marketplace platform eng
- "During canary we saw silent fallback to smaller model and it wasn't obvious why." — product manager at B2B SaaS

Grouped asks (compact)
1) KV cache & session handling
- Symptom: Periodic token cost spikes when customers reuse short prefixes across many sessions.
- Ask: Expose cache-hit ratio per customer + per-route over rolling 1h window. Add optional sticky-session affinity for model/KV routing.
- Short fix: Add a lightweight prefix-frequency gauge to the console (top 20 prefixes) + alert template.
- Impact estimate: medium cost savings (10–25% token reduction for affected flows).

2) Per-route cost preview and soft-quota tooling
- Symptom: Teams fear burst bills after enabling high-throughput routes.
- Ask: Allow simulated 24h cost preview using current traffic shape + conservative quantization profiles. Add soft-cap alarms and pre-approval flow.
- Short fix: UI button: "Estimate 24h spend for X TPS" that replays traffic distribution.
- Impact: reduces support escalations and contract friction.

3) Rollout transparency and deterministic fallback
- Symptom: Customers see silent model fallbacks without clear reason (quota, instabilities).
- Ask: Provide an event stream for rollout decisions (why request routed to variant B). Include a policy trace link with decision tags: capacity, latency_slo, cost_tier.
- Short fix: Add a debug toggle that attaches a small policy-decisions header to responses for dev/test environments.

4) Private deployment onboarding checklist
- Symptom: Multiple stalled installs due to VPC peering, egress rules, and KMS permissions.
- Ask: Short runbook with minimal network policies + preflight validator.
- Short fix: Share a single-page network diagram and a terraform snippet customers can run to validate.

5) Streaming chunk edge cases and function-calling retries
- Symptom: Partial function-call outputs when clients reconnect; retries lead to duplicated side-effects.
- Ask: Add an idempotency token option for function calls and a server-side resume token for streams.
- Short fix: Expose a header to opt into idempotent execution for function endpoints.

Quick experiments and low-effort patches (<=1 sprint)
- Console: "Top prefixes" gauge and per-route cache-hit ratio card (frontend + metric API).
- API: optional Response-Decision header in dev mode (exposes routing reasons).
- Docs: Single-page VPC preflight + terraform check.
- Billing: Lightweight cost-replay button for route previews.

Open questions for product/eng
- What privacy constraints limit exposing prefix summaries? (need legal/infosec check)
- Can we attach policy decision traces without increasing response latency? (trace sampling?)
- What rollout for idempotency semantics with existing function-calling? (compat concerns)

Next steps / who to own what
- CS: Aisha to collect top 8 customer examples and attach logs to JIRA-1842 (due 2026-06-14).
- Eng (serving runtime): Liam to scope header debug toggle + estimate perf delta (sprint 26.3).
- Product: Marta to draft requirements for cost-preview flow; coordinate with billing.
- Docs & Solutions: Devon to assemble the VPC preflight and terraform validator; publish to partner onboarding repo.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this compact; customers need confidence fast. Prioritize observable wins that reduce support load over perfect long-term solutions.
- We should A/B the cost-preview UI with a small cohort to confirm it lowers pre-sale blocker rates.

Attachments / raw links (will add logs to JIRA)
- Will append collected logs and a small sample policy trace for 3 customers in JIRA-1842.

End.
